bull.b: Having three programs in Phase III creates multiple potential paths toward regulatory approval and future commercialization. The defined BLA schedule supports a durable development strategy, while diversification across retinal diseases may reduce reliance on a single clinical asset.

The OCU400 licensing agreement expands commercial reach without requiring Ocugen to independently build a full regional infrastructure. Upfront payments, milestones, royalties, and supply revenue provide potential non-dilutive economics if development and commercialization progress.

A cash runway extending into 2028 gives Ocugen time to generate clinical data and pursue regulatory milestones before needing additional capital. This supports execution of key late-stage programs and provides greater planning visibility during the development cycle.

bear.b: Ocugen remains a clinical-stage company with very limited revenue and no demonstrated scalable profitability. Persistent negative margins mean future operations depend on financing, partnerships, or successful product approvals rather than internally generated earnings.

Substantial recurring cash outflows show that the business is not self-funding its research and development activities. Continued burn can consume available resources before commercialization and increase dependence on external capital or milestone-based funding.

Negative equity combined with sharply higher debt reduces financial flexibility and increases the consequences of continued losses. The balance-sheet structure may constrain investment choices and heighten refinancing or dilution risk as the pipeline advances.
